assessment.nobel_worthiness: A decisive, lasting framework for treating local electronic correlations beyond ordinary band theory. Its ability to connect correlated-electron models with measured material spectra is particularly compelling.
assessment.attribution: Georges and Kotliar developed the self-consistent dynamical mapping; Vollhardt supplied the infinite-dimensional foundations. This trio represents a coherent theoretical achievement.
assessment.maturity: A mature framework with decades of use and extensive comparison with correlated-material experiments.
uncertainties: The packet supplies no contribution chronology; the role of other foundational collaborators needs examination. Approximate implementations must not be confused with universally exact material predictions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Established a new organizing principle for electronic matter: robust boundary conduction fixed by time-reversal-invariant band topology. It combines original theory with a sharply testable material realization.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele represent the theoretical identification and classification; Molenkamp represents the quantum-spin-Hall realization. The supplied trio supports a focused configuration.
assessment.maturity: The core phase and its characteristic boundary physics are established and have generated a sustained materials program.
uncertainties: The packet does not distinguish the historical credit for two-dimensional and three-dimensional realizations; the prize citation should remain focused.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Spin-dependent tunnelling made magnetism a practical control variable in electronic devices. The combination of quantum transport physics and durable technological use is Nobel-scale.
assessment.attribution: Moodera and Miyazaki represent independent room-temperature demonstrations; Parkin represents the later high-performance junction development. A precise citation must separate these contributions.
assessment.maturity: Long-established physics with extensive device use and independent material implementations.
uncertainties: Credit for crystalline-barrier theory and parallel experiments is not described; the fairness of adding the later development to the original discovery needs review.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: A striking prediction-and-discovery sequence that turns twist angle into a design variable for interacting quantum matter. It changed how theorists and experimentalists construct model materials.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald represent the magic-angle band prediction; Jarillo-Herrero represents the correlated-insulator and superconducting discovery. The supplied trio is coherent.
assessment.maturity: The flat-band platform and correlated phases are established; the detailed mechanism of its superconductivity remains less settled.
uncertainties: A citation should recognize the experimentally established platform rather than assert a settled pairing mechanism. Device fabrication and parallel observational credit need examination.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Zero-field quantized Hall transport connects magnetic order, electronic structure and topology in a concrete material. It is an unusually clear theoretical-to-experimental discovery.
assessment.attribution: Dai and Fang represent the material-specific theoretical route; Xue represents the experimental realization. Their complementary roles support a focused prize.
assessment.maturity: The integer quantized effect has had substantial time for independent investigation and refinement.
uncertainties: The packet lacks transport-quality evidence and a full history of the theoretical prediction; low-temperature and materials limitations should be distinguished from validity of the discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magnetic skyrmions reveal topological structure and emergent electrodynamics in real magnets, joining spin theory to measurable textures and transport.
assessment.attribution: Pfleiderer and Tokura represent experimental establishment and material development; Rosch represents theoretical interpretation. The division is plausible but requires documentary support.
assessment.maturity: The principal textures are mature experimental objects studied by multiple methods and in multiple systems.
uncertainties: Prediction, first observation and emergent-electrodynamic signatures are distinct credit questions; the sparse packet cannot establish that this trio covers every decisive originator.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: A major semiconductor and energy-materials advance with unusual optoelectronic performance. Recognition is attractive where a clear physical discovery underlies its extraordinary utility.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka represents the initial photovoltaic use; Park and Snaith the efficient solid-state implementations. The supplied names form a plausible progression.
assessment.maturity: The photovoltaic capability is well established and extensively reproduced; long-term device durability is a separate issue.
uncertainties: The packet does not isolate a single fundamental mechanism from successive device advances, or establish comparative priority. Energy usefulness alone cannot determine the citation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Made strongly interacting lattice Hamiltonians into controllable laboratory systems, allowing theory to be tested in regimes inaccessible to routine calculation.
assessment.attribution: Zoller represents the lattice-model proposal; Bloch and Greiner represent the decisive many-body realization and imaging program. This subset keeps theory and experiment together.
assessment.maturity: The core Hubbard-model simulation and Mott-transition achievements have a long, reproducible experimental history.
uncertainties: Dalibard and Cirac are also credited in the packet. Their precise indispensable contributions, versus later extensions, must be assessed before fixing a three-person allocation.
